summary: Pitch correction for a single voice or a melodic line. It follows the pitch of the input, moves it to the nearest note of a key and scale (or to the notes a MIDI keyboard holds) at a chosen speed, and re-synthesises the sound (by resampling and splicing whole periods for small corrections, by pitch-synchronous overlap-add when the formants or a large transpose are used), so the timbre stays the singer's. The Natural control is the main knob: 0 % is the hard tune effect, 100 % a transparent correction that moves only the centre of each settled note and leaves the vibrato; it sets the fine controls (Retune speed, Correction zone, Keep vibrato, Humanize, Transition, Note stickiness), which can be edited after. Retune speed 0 is the hard, robotic effect, a slower speed leaves the glide between notes; Humanize and Keep singer's vibrato leave the natural drift and vibrato of held notes; Amount blends the correction in. Formant preserve keeps the vowel colour when the pitch moves, Formant shift changes it for deeper or smaller voices, Transpose moves the whole voice by up to two octaves, Add vibrato puts a steady vibrato on a flat note. Range picks the tracker and the latency: Low latency (voices above 100 Hz, about 10 ms, for live use), Quality (about 28 ms) or Full (down to bass, about 36 ms); the latency is reported to NeoBuzz Live. Unvoiced sounds (breaths, s and t) and silence pass through unchanged. Use it on a lead vocal, a harmony or a solo instrument that has one note at a time.
use_for: Pitch correction for a lead vocal or a solo line: moves the voice to a key and scale (or to MIDI notes), hard or natural, with formant control, transpose and added vibrato.

parameters.name: Key from
parameters.description: Set: the key and scale below. Listen: the key is worked out from the notes sung so far (the app has no song-wide key yet)
parameters.how: Chooses where the key comes from: the Key and Scale controls (Set), or the notes the machine has heard (Listen; the scale type stays as set).
parameters.sound: Listen lets the voice settle into the key it already sings in, which suits a first draft; Set is exact.

parameters.name: Key
parameters.description: The root note of the scale (ignored for Chromatic and Custom)
parameters.how: Sets the root note of the scale, C to B.
parameters.sound: Moves the allowed notes up or down so they fit the song's key.

parameters.name: Scale
parameters.description: Which notes the voice may land on; Custom uses the 12-note mask (click the keys in the editor)
parameters.how: Chooses the set of allowed notes: chromatic (all 12), the major, minor and church modes, harmonic minor, the pentatonics, blues, or a custom mask.
parameters.sound: Fewer notes pull harder and sound more obviously corrected; Chromatic only fixes the voice to the nearest semitone.

parameters.name: Custom notes
parameters.description: Custom note mask: bit n is pitch class n, C = bit 0 (default C major); used when Scale is Custom
parameters.how: The twelve notes of the Custom scale as a number: C is 1, C sharp 2, D 4 and so on, added together.
parameters.sound: Allows exactly the notes you click in the editor's keyboard, in every octave.

parameters.name: Retune speed
parameters.description: How fast the pitch moves to the note: 0 ms is instant (hard), 400 ms is a slow glide
parameters.how: Sets how long the voice takes to reach the target note, from 0 to 400 ms.
parameters.sound: 0 gives the hard, stepped robotic sound; 20 to 80 ms sounds natural; the longest lets the voice slide between notes.

parameters.name: Humanize
parameters.description: How much of a held note's own slow drift is kept
parameters.how: Sets how much of the singer's slow drift around a held note stays, from 0 to 100 %.
parameters.sound: At 0 a held note is dead flat; higher values keep it alive and human.

parameters.name: Amount
parameters.description: How much of the correction is applied: 0 % leaves the voice as sung, 100 % moves it fully to the note
parameters.how: Blends the correction in, from 0 to 100 % of the distance to the note (in cents).
parameters.sound: Lower values tune the voice only part of the way, which hides the effect.

parameters.name: Transpose
parameters.description: Moves the whole voice up or down by whole semitones, after the correction
parameters.how: Moves the corrected voice by whole semitones, from -24 to +24.
parameters.sound: An octave up or down gives a different voice; the formant setting decides if it stays a human size.

parameters.name: Formant preserve
parameters.description: On: the vowel colour stays where it was when the pitch moves. Off: the vowel colour moves with the pitch (a sped-up or slowed voice)
parameters.how: Keeps the spectral envelope (the vowel) in place while the pitch changes, or lets it follow the pitch.
parameters.sound: On sounds like the same person singing another note; off sounds like a smaller or larger singer.

parameters.name: Formant shift
parameters.description: Moves the vowel colour by whole semitones, up for a smaller voice, down for a larger one
parameters.how: Shifts the formants (the vowel colour) by -12 to +12 semitones, on top of Formant preserve.
parameters.sound: Up makes a younger or smaller character, down a deeper and heavier one; the extremes turn robotic.

parameters.name: Keep vibrato
parameters.description: How much of the singer's own vibrato stays in the corrected voice
parameters.how: Passes the fast pitch movement of the singer's vibrato through the correction, from 0 to 100 %.
parameters.sound: At 0 the hard correction flattens every vibrato; at 100 % it stays as sung.

parameters.name: Add vibrato
parameters.description: Depth of a steady vibrato added on a held note
parameters.how: Adds an even vibrato of 0 to 100 cents on top of the corrected note.
parameters.sound: Gives a plain, tuned note some life; zero adds nothing.

parameters.name: Vibrato rate
parameters.description: Speed of the added vibrato
parameters.how: Sets the speed of the added vibrato from 0.5 to 9 Hz.
parameters.sound: Around 5 to 6 Hz sounds like a singer; slower is a gentle wave.

parameters.name: Vibrato delay
parameters.description: How long a note is held before the added vibrato fades in
parameters.how: Sets the time after a new note before the added vibrato starts, from 0 to 1000 ms.
parameters.sound: Singers start a note straight and add vibrato later; this copies that.

parameters.name: Target
parameters.description: Scale: the notes of the key and scale. MIDI: the notes held on the machine's MIDI input (the key and scale are ignored)
parameters.how: Chooses what the voice is moved to: the scale's notes, or the notes held on the MIDI input.
parameters.sound: MIDI lets a keyboard or a clip conduct the voice, and with a chord held it picks the nearest chord tone.

parameters.name: MIDI octave
parameters.description: Nearest: a held note counts in every octave, so the voice stays in its own range. Exact: only the octave played
parameters.how: In MIDI mode, whether a held note counts in all octaves (Nearest) or only the one played (Exact).
parameters.sound: Nearest keeps the voice where it was and just changes the note; Exact makes the voice sing the played pitch.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: Low latency: voices above 100 Hz, about 10 ms. Quality: voices above 70 Hz, about 28 ms. Full: down to bass, about 36 ms. The latency is reported to the app
parameters.how: Picks the pitch tracker and the grain length, and with them the latency: 10, 28 or 36 ms.
parameters.sound: Low latency is for playing live and a little less steady on low voices; Quality is the best sound; Full also follows bass voices and instruments.

parameters.name: Input
parameters.description: Which channel the voice is taken from: the sum of left and right, or the left channel only
parameters.how: Chooses the input: the two channels added, or the left channel only.
parameters.sound: The corrected voice is always mono; the dry sound stays in stereo.

parameters.name: Transients
parameters.description: Keeps the sharp start of a sound (a b, d or p) as sung instead of re-synthesising it
parameters.how: Lets the first few milliseconds of a hard consonant or a plucked note pass through unprocessed.
parameters.sound: On keeps consonants crisp; off treats them like the rest of the voice.

parameters.name: Mix
parameters.description: Wet against dry; at 0 % the output is the delayed input, bit for bit
parameters.how: Blends the corrected voice with the original (delayed to match).
parameters.sound: Parallel use keeps the character of the singer while the tuning shows through.

parameters.name: Natural
parameters.description: How natural the correction sounds: 0 % is the hard, robotic effect, 100 % is a transparent correction that keeps the singer's expression. Moving it sets Retune speed, Correction zone, Keep vibrato, Humanize, Transition and Note stickiness together
parameters.how: Sets how natural the correction sounds, from the hard effect (0 %) to a transparent one (100 %). In the editor it rewrites the fine controls below it in one step; they can then be edited by hand.
parameters.sound: 0 % snaps every note flat and instant; about 40 % is a pop polish; about 75 % corrects the centre of each note and leaves the vibrato, scoops and glides; 100 % is as transparent as it gets.

parameters.name: Correction zone
parameters.description: How far from a note the correction still pulls: movement outside the zone passes through as sung (100 cents and more: no zone, every pitch is corrected)
parameters.how: Sets the zone around each note, from 0 to 100 cents, within which the correction applies; fades out beyond it.
parameters.sound: A narrow zone lets scoops, slides and expressive bends through and corrects only the pitch that settles near a note; 100 corrects everything.

parameters.name: Transition
parameters.description: Between notes: 0 % snaps at the midpoint, 100 % leaves the singer's own glide untouched
parameters.how: Sets how note changes are handled, from a snap (0 %) to the singer's own glide kept (100 %): the correction fades while the pitch of the note centre is moving fast.
parameters.sound: Snap sounds like the effect; glide keeps slides between notes as sung.

parameters.name: Note stickiness
parameters.description: How hard it is to leave a note: how far past the midpoint, and for how long, the pitch has to be before the target changes
parameters.how: Sets the hysteresis (in cents past the midpoint) and the minimum time before the target note changes, from low (0 %) to high (100 %).
parameters.sound: High stickiness stops a wide vibrato or a wobble from flipping between neighbouring notes; low follows quick note changes.

parameters.name: Method
parameters.description: Auto: period splicing for small corrections, PSOLA when formants or a large transpose are used. Splice or PSOLA: always that engine
parameters.how: Chooses how the sound is re-synthesised: Auto, the splice engine (resample and repeat or drop whole periods, the most transparent) or PSOLA (grains, with formant control).
parameters.sound: Splice keeps the singer's voice almost untouched for corrections under about 2 semitones; PSOLA can move formants and transpose widely.

readings.description: The pitch of the voice now, Hz (0 when not voiced)
The note the voice is moved to, as a MIDI number (0 when not voiced)
How far the correction moves the pitch now, cents (negative: down)
1 while a pitch is found, 0 for unvoiced sounds and silence
The delay of the machine, reported to NeoBuzz Live
